info.title: CanyonOS API
info.description: Each workflow group has its own API key, the one it was deployed with, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and checked before the request is read: a request without it is 401 whatever it sends. A workflow group deployed with no key is open. The requests, metrics, monitoring, prompts, scaling, governance, history and sample-data routes of a workflow under /v1/workflow-groups/<workflow_group_id> take that workflow group's key; a workflow group this API has no record of is 401. /v1/workflows and /v1/resources answer with the workflows of the workflow groups the key opens and of the open ones; a key that opens none of the workflow groups that have one is 401. /v1/auth/check answers 200 to a key that opens a workflow group, and to anyone while none has a key. The telemetry routes of a workflow group (POST traces, metrics and logs under /v1/workflow-groups/<workflow_group_id>) take no key: the Global Controller that sends them holds none. On Docker every other /v1/workflow-groups route takes the machine's deploy key (the sha256 of which is CANYONOS_DEPLOY_KEY_HASH) or the workflow group's own key, and is open on a workflow group with none; a workflow group this API has no record of yet takes the deploy key only, and the list shows each caller the workflow groups its key opens, the deploy key every one. On Kubernetes (CANYONOS_TARGET=kubernetes) each of those routes needs the Kubernetes login of its caller as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and a route on a workflow group needs the right to get (to read) or update (to change) CanyonProjects in its namespace. Until its database is migrated and answers, every route that reads it, the key checks included, answers 503 `database.unavailable`; /v1/readyz says when the API is ready.

get.summary: Health Check
Ready once the database is migrated and answers; also says whether Docker does
Whether any workflow group needs a key; asked before sign-in
get.description: True too while the database is not ready to say.

get.summary: Answers 200 when the key opens a workflow group; what sign-in checks a key with
get.description: Also 200 with no key while no workflow group has one; 401 `auth.missing_key` or `auth.invalid_key` otherwise.

get.summary: Fleet overview: per-workflow cost/requests/tokens over a time range
get.description: Counts the requests that started in the range, each whole, of the workflows of the workflow groups the key opens, the open ones included.

get.summary: List the workflow groups
get.description: Every workflow group with an upload here or a deploy (a Global Controller container on Docker, a CanyonProject on Kubernetes), with the name its last PUT gave it, empty before one. On Docker, the machine's deploy key lists every one; any other caller the workflow groups its key opens and the open ones.

put.description: Writes `workflow_group.yaml` and the `.env` beside it into the workflow group's workspace, removing that `.env` when `env` is null, and keeps `name` as the workflow group's name. With `workflows`, removes the uploaded workflows it leaves out; with `api_key_hash`, keeps it as the API key its endpoint checks, none when it is empty. On Docker, 409 `controller_missing` when the CLI has not created the Global Controller container. On Kubernetes, 403 unless the caller may update CanyonProjects in the namespace `config` names, and 409 `reupload_needed` for a PUT without `workflows` while the API holds none of the workflows, as after it restarted.

delete.summary: Stop the deploy and forget the upload
delete.description: Waits for the apply loop to stop the deploy, then forgets the upload; 504 when it did not stop in time and 500 when stopping it failed, keeping the upload. A deploy this API holds no upload for is stopped all the same.

get.summary: Read the workflow group's status
get.description: The workflow group's name and `workflow_group.yaml` as last uploaded, how far the apply loop got, the deploy's phase, progress and verdict, and while it runs, its endpoint, agents and machine errors; a part that could not be read is left null and named under `errors`.

put.description: Checks the gzip tar of the workflow as `canyonos validate` does, then unpacks it into the workflow group's workspace, removing what its last upload had and this one lacks; on a 400 (bad archive, unsafe path or findings) the old files stay. 404 when the uploaded `workflow_group.yaml` gives no workflow this workflow_id.

requestBody.description: A gzip tar of the workflow's folder, paths relative to it, with its `.env`

delete.description: Removes from the workflow group's workspace what the workflow's last upload put there; 404 if it was never uploaded.

get.summary: List the uploaded workflows
Read a workflow's agent graph
get.description: Which agents each agent of the workflow can call, and each call between them with the earlier calls it waits for, read from its code without running it when it was last uploaded. Whether a call runs, how often, and its order beyond that are what a request's trace shows. 404 `unknown_workflow` if it was never uploaded, `graph_unavailable` if its code couldn't be read then or it was uploaded before the API read graphs.

get.summary: Read the controller log
get.description: The deploy's log, the last `tail` lines of it, as text; with `follow=true`, keeps streaming new lines until the deploy stops. On Docker, the Global Controller container's log since it last started; on Kubernetes, the build pod's while it builds, then the Global Controller pod's. Empty before there is one.

get.summary: Read an agent's replica logs
get.description: The last `tail` lines of each running replica of the agent whose ID is `agent_id`, or of the one replica whose ID it is, read on its machine; 409 if the deploy is not running, 404 naming the agents when it is neither, 503 when its Redis cannot be read.

get.summary: Check the running deploy
get.description: Checks the running deploy's Global Controller, Redis, each agent's replica count and its endpoint, each with how to fix it when it fails; 409 if it is not running.

put.summary: Register the workflow group's workflows with this dashboard
put.description: Stores each workflow's name by its workflow_id with the workflow group's Redis: its container name, port and password, and a client certificate its CA signs when it takes only TLS. `canyonos deploy` sends it once the Global Controller container exists, before it starts: nothing connects to the Redis here; the status and the dashboard read it once the deploy runs. Returns the workflows as the dashboard names them; a workflow registered before keeps its name. A workflow of another workflow group moves in only when the caller opens that one too: with its key, the deploy key, or while it has no key; 409 `registry.workflow_taken` otherwise. On Docker, 404 without the workflow group's container or upload. On Kubernetes the operator's registry already lists the workflow group: the body is optional and not used, and the workflows the dashboard knows of it are returned; on Docker a request without it is 422 `workflow_groups.registration_required`.

post.summary: Add the recorded example run to this workflow
post.description: Replays a run of the named bundled workflow that this API ships, spread across the week ending now, so a first run opens a dashboard with history rather than one request. The body names a workflow, never data: the only rows it can write are its own. Repeatable, and it never touches rows the workflow produced itself.
